2.Heard learned counsel for the applicant and learned Additional Government Advocate for the State.
As per instructions provided by learned A.G.A., notice to respondent No.4 has been served.
3.It is alleged in the prosecution case that the applicant was residing with his relative Gayadeen.

On 18.5.2022, he along with the deceased was found on the roof of the house of deceased by the informant, uncle and cousin of the deceased Pohkar and Aditya and they both were taken downwards in the house and feeling humiliated by the incident, the deceased had bolted herself in a room from inside and hanged herself.
4.In the post mortem report, cause of death is asphyxia as a result of ante mortem hanging.
Initially, the first information report was lodged under section 306 I.P.C., in which the applicant has been released on bail vide order dated 14.2.2023 passed in Bail No.9183 of 2022 (Annexure-9).

During investigation, FSL report had come in which spermatozoa in the vaginal smear slide has been found and Sections 376 I.P.C.
and 3/4 POCSO Act have been added.

5.Learned counsel for the applicant has drawn attention of this Court towards statement of the complainant and submitted that no allegation of rape was levelled by the complainant in the first information report nor in the statement under Section 161 CrPC.
It was not the case of the prosecution in the first information report or in the statement of the complainant that the victim was raped.

It is submitted that the two eye witnesses Ponkar and Ramkali who were family members of the deceased have made improvement contrary to the initial version of the first information report and the statement of the complainant.
No material has been collected by the investigating officer regarding minority of the victim.
Both were having consensual relationship for a long time.
Only because they were caught by the family members, the victim suffered humiliation and committed suicide.
No offence under sections 376 I.P.C. and 3/4 POCSO Act is made out.
The applicant has been falsely implicated.
Learned counsel for the applicant undertakes that the applicant shall cooperate in the trial.
6. Learned Addl.

Government Advocate has opposed the prayer made by applicant's counsel, however, he has fairly submitted that the investigating officer apart from the statement of the complainant that the victim is 17 years old has not collected any other material to find out minority of the victim.

8.Considering the above aspects of the matter, perusal of the record, prima facie there appears to be no allegation of rape in the first information report or in the statement of the complainant, the applicant has already incarcerated in jail for about nine months, as also the judgment in Sushila Aggarwal and others versus State (NCT of Delhi) and another (2020)5 SCC 1 and without entering into the merit of the case,
it would be appropriate to grant interim protection to the applicant under Section 438 Cr.P.C.

sentences.text: Till the next date of listing, it is provided that in the event of arrest, the applicant shall be released on anticipatory bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial court.
The applicant shall cooperate in the trial and he will not influence the witnesses.
Any other condition which the trial court may deem fit and proper may be imposed.
10. In case of default, it would be open for the trial court to proceed against the applicant as per law."
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is cooperating in the trial.
He has not flouted any condition enumerated in the order dated 23.02.2023.
Learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the bail application.

On due consideration to the fact that the applicant has already incarcerated for a period of nine months in jail till his release on 24.02.2023 as well as considering the fact that the applicant is cooperating in the trial and he has not flouted the conditions enumerated in the order whereby he was granted interim protection, the interim protection granted vide order dated 21.08.2024 is made absolute in view of dictum of Apex Court in re: Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi)-2020 SCC online SC 98.

opennyai_summary.decision:
Till the next date of listing, it is provided that in the event of arrest, the applicant shall be released on anticipatory bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial court.
The applicant shall cooperate in the trial and he will not influence the witnesses.
Any other condition which the trial court may deem fit and proper may be imposed.
10. In case of default, it would be open for the trial court to proceed against the applicant as per law."
He has not flouted any condition enumerated in the order dated 23.02.2023.
On due consideration to the fact that the applicant has already incarcerated for a period of nine months in jail till his release on 24.02.2023 as well as considering the fact that the applicant is cooperating in the trial and he has not flouted the conditions enumerated in the order whereby he was granted interim protection, the interim protection granted vide order dated 21.08.2024 is made absolute in view of dictum of Apex Court in re: Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi)-2020 SCC online SC 98.
In view of the above, since, charge-sheet in the matter has been filed, if the applicant is summoned to face trial for offence in question, he shall be released on bail by the trial court on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties of the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall not, directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the court or tamper with the evidence;
(ii) The applicant shall not leave India without the previous permission of the court;
(iv)The applicant shall appear before the trial court on each date fixed unless personal presence is exempted;
(v) In case of breach of any of the above conditions the court below shall have the liberty to cancel the bail;
Any other reasonable restrictions/conditions which the trial court may deem fit and proper can be imposed.
It is made clear that the observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
In view of the aforesaid, the application is allowed.
